chapter: Postwar Chicago, Janis and De Paris
title: Chicago's Blue Note with Art Hodes; George Brunis forces him out
summary: With Hodes's eight-piece band he was dismissed after eight weeks when George Brunis objected to him singing Ugly Child; Zutty Singleton followed and was also fired.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Now, let's... You worked in Chicago with Art Hodes around 1950. Did you go to Chicago with Hodes? Or did he send for you? Was he out there already at that time? How did you end up in Chicago?
Well, he got a band together. I think the band was made up in New York. I don't just remember... No, it

wasn't made in New York. He got the men at a place called...not the Savoy, but some big club...some big club down in Chicago... The Blue Note? No... Maybe it was the Blue Note. Yeah, yeah, the Blue Note.
The Blue Note was an established club there that had been around a while.

Yeah. The Blue Note, yeah. That was on the second floor, the second or third floor, the Blue Note. We had an eight piece band. We were supposed to be there sixteen weeks. I guess it was around eight weeks at the Savoy... They had a drummer by the name of George Brunis in the band. He recorded that number "Ugly Child."
He recorded that, I think it was Decca, a Decca recording, "Ugly Child."
Now, is this the George Brunis, the New Orleans trombone player, or another George with a similar name.
There was only one, one George Brunis. That was George Brunis.
He was kind of hard to get along with. And he come in the band... Well, he was in the band when it first started. And I made the... Otherwise, he did that "Ugly

Child." But I was doing it in New York. See, everybody liked the way I do it. See, I was doing "Ugly Child" out there, and George Brunis didn't like that so well, you know? So he made a spectacle he was going to leave the band if Freddie Moore is still going to stay in the band and sing my number. So you know how them boys will work together, you know. So I had to go. He kept George Brunis. Said the boss who owned the place, he liked George Brunis, one of them things. Out I went after eight weeks.
They got another drummer. I forget who the other drummer was... Zutty Singleton.

Yeah, they had Zutty. Zutty Singleton and Art Hodes got to fighting backstage about something. I don't know, they were tearing the place down in the back. Out he went! And they got another drummer, they got the house boy in Chicago to finish out...you know...
